root.docs:
# ePA Authentication Lab — Milestone 1

Both folders are included: **idp** (Keycloak/OIDC) and **epa-authorization** (NestJS).
Dev targets the current LAN server. Stag and prod contain editable HTTPS placeholders.
Run OIDC discovery first; endpoints are taken from its response, never guessed.

The IDP sequence is discovery → JWKS → pushed authorization request → login form.
Direct PAR requires a locally supplied OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET. The backend sequence needs no
client secret in this API client: the NestJS server authenticates its own PAR request.
The backend authorization response stays at HTTP 302; AUTHORIZATION_URL contains the
short-lived browser link. Open it immediately and once. The IDP login-form request consumes
the reference generated by direct PAR. Obtain a new reference before repeating it.

No login submission, code callback, token exchange, user session or admin API is implemented
in this milestone. The registered dev callback remains http://localhost:3000/callback even
when the two servers are accessed over LAN. Changing it requires registration at both servers.
Negative requests document the current Milestone 1 contract.

TLS verification stays enabled. Credentials and generated Basic authentication are never
written to these export files. Clear IDP cookies before testing if already logged in.
See the repository README for import, mode selection and parameter instructions.

Bruno: select the included dev, stag or prod environment. Edit its parameters before use. OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET is a blank secret variable; set it locally. The CLI may alternatively read DEV_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, STAG_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET or PROD_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET from its process environment. Compatible with Safe Mode; no Developer Mode is required.

Standalone environment files are also provided in docs/api-clients/environments/dev.bru, stag.bru and prod.bru. Copy them into the imported collection's environments directory to restore the included profiles, then select the desired environment. For the CLI, use --env-file with the path to the desired .bru file.

request.docs: Direct IDP smoke test. Set OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET locally for the selected deployment. Uses client_secret_basic and fresh PKCE, state and nonce. Saves AUTHORIZATION_URL. The verifier is not retained because M1 stops at the login form.

headers.name: Accept
headers.description: Keycloak browser login page.

request.docs: Use immediately after a successful PAR. Follows up to three internal IDP redirects with the cookie jar to display the real Keycloak login form. Consumes this short-lived reference; repeat PAR for a new one. Clear IDP cookies if already signed in. Do not submit credentials: no callback is implemented.

headers.description: Optional guest mode; unsupported in M1 (403 invalAuth). Both guest headers together are invalid (400).

headers.description: Optional eGK guest mode; unsupported in M1 (403 invalAuth). Omit rather than send false.

request.docs: Header-only GET. Sends a genuine PAR through the backend and returns 302 with client_id and request_uri only. Automatic redirects are disabled. Saves AUTHORIZATION_URL for immediate manual browser use. IDP discovery is needed for the collection assertions; the backend discovers independently. No client secret is sent to NestJS.
